newsitem.title: USA: Protection One targets growth after deal.
newsitem.headline: Protection One targets growth after deal.

text.p: Protection One Inc said Thursday it anticipates plenty of acquisition opportunities after merging with Western Resources Inc in the latest transaction to hit the fragmented electronic security sector.
The deal, announced on Wednesday, would create a significant industry player competing with Tyco International Ltd, which recently bought industry leader ADT Ltd.
West Coast-based Protection One previously had expressed interest in joining with another company to capture a piece of the booming security market.

"In the next 24 months, there are a number of significant properties which may become available in the marketplace which will even accelerate (previously-anticipated) growth," said Protection One Chief Financial Officer John Hesse in a telephone conference call.

Kansas utility Western Resources recently lost its effort to buy ADT and had vowed to expand its burgeoning role in electronic security through acquisitions. The company last year bought the electronic security business of Westinghouse Corp and has been viewed as having plenty of potential partners in the consolidating industry.
Utilities are increasingly interested in electronic security as a means to expand outside the typically slow-growth industry that is in the throes of deregulation.

The latest transaction calls for Western Resources to pay $320 million to Protection One in exchange for an 80.1 percent stake in Protection One. Shareholders of Protection would receive a special dividend of $7.00 a share after the deal closed and continue to own 19.9 percent of the company.
The two companies would combine their electronic security businesses under the Protection One name. Western's security unit now operates under the Westar name.
Hesse said the two firms began preliminary talks in January at an industry conference in Florida. Talks then accelerated when Western lost its effort to buy ADT, he said.

He also assured investors that Protection One's top management will remain with the company. The plan calls for Protection One officials to run the new company, along with Westar executive Steven Millstein.

"The reason we, being the managemnt, chose this transaction as opposed to pursuing others that may have been available to us is that the current management team has the opportunity to manage and grow this larger business," Hesse said.

"A lot of our net worth is tied up in the future of this company. I can't give any ironclad guarantees...but there are no plans for any of us to leave this company in the near future or in the intermediate term," he said.
